title: Rack surge margin and deployment phasing playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working playbook for planning on-prem and colocated GPU rack deployments when we expect short-term surges and phased capacity rollouts. Focus areas: electrical safety margin, cooling headroom by aisle, physical slot staging, and operations handoff for phased installs.

High-level goals:
- Keep per-rack steady-state power below 70% of breaker capacity to preserve N+1 headroom for surge and maintenance.
- Define a 3-phase deployment pattern so we can stagger installs, avoid hot-aisle thermal shocks, and enable safe failover to neighboring racks when a pod is hot-swapped.
- Provide a checklist that SRE/Field Ops can run in a 90-minute window during rack bringup.

Assumptions used for quick modeling (modify per site):
- Standard rack breaker: 63A at 3-phase, 208V (nominal).
- Usable continuous power per rack (derated): 30 kW.
- Target steady-state per-rack GPU draw (initial config): 18 kW (includes PDUs, switches, ~15kW for 8x high-density nodes + 3kW base).
- PUE local assumed: 1.25 (edge sites may be higher).
- Cooling transient capacity: facility provides +25% short-term headroom for 15 minutes.
- Expected short-term surge window: 10–30 minutes during model warm-up or batch workloads.
- Temperature ops threshold: inlet target 18–27°C, emergency at 35°C inlet.

Scenario matrix (quick view):
| Scenario | Rack draw (kW) | Fraction of breaker | Action | Cooling reserve needed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| Normal steady | 18 | 60% | OK | 25% available reserve |
| 1.2x surge | 21.6 | 72% | Alert + throttle policies | 10% reserve, monitor inlet |
| 1.4x surge | 25.2 | 84% | Spill to neighbor racks, enable throttling | 0% reserve — risk of inlet rise |
| Failure of one CDU | 36 (two racks combined) | 120% (over breaker) | Immediate evacuation / firmware limit | Not possible — require manual action |

Key operational tolerances and rules of thumb:
- Do not exceed 80% of usable continuous power for more than 5 minutes; rely on routing/burst policies to cap tokenized work.
- Maintain at least 10% cooling headroom for short surges (thermal inertia typically buys 10–15 minutes).
- For high-density racks (>20 kW steady), require additional CRAC cooling feed or move to staggered intake baffles.
- Where available, use per-rack inlet sensors + PDU telemetry to trigger automated throttles in Redwood serving router.

Phased deployment plan (3 phases):
Phase A — Pilot (1–2 racks):
- Purpose: validate power metering accuracy, PDU firmware, thermal behavior with representative models (seq length 512/2048).
- Actions: install 1 rack, run 4-hour soak with synthetic traffic + KV cache warm-up, log inlet/outlet temps and PDU currents every 30s.
- Acceptance: inlet < 28°C and no trips; PDU telemetry within ±5% of clamp metering.

Phase B — Incremental scale (add 3–6 racks over 2 weeks):
- Purpose: observe cross-aisle interactions and validate spill routing across racks.
- Actions: deploy 2 racks, wait 24h, deploy remaining; enable traffic shaping default to 0.8x for first 72h to limit surge exposure.
- Acceptance: no CDU trips, CPU/GPU throttles engaged at expected thresholds, emergency escalation OK.

Phase C — Full capacity (continuous fleet scale):
- Purpose: transition to production throughput; onsite ops to run day/night shift for first 72h to handle thermal drift.
- Actions: progressive rollout with monitoring runbook; set SLI triggers for automated rollback.

Physical slotting & space considerations:
- Staging: reserve adjacent empty rack slots to act as "cool spill"; do not populate contiguous racks with hottest nodes during first pass.
- Cable density: use staggered power strip insertion to prevent bus imbalance on PDUs. Tag PDUs with colored tape and document mapping in rack diagram.
- Exhaust flow: ensure no blockage in top-of-rack (TOR) cable trays; route vertical fiber outside hot-aisle.

Bringup checklist (90-minute window):
1) Verify power feed labeling, breaker capacity, and PDU serials match manifest.
2) Cable management: verify hot-aisle exhaust clear, no bundled cables > 30% cross-section.
3) Flash PDUs to approved firmware (see linked GH PR).
4) Meter baseline idle currents for every PDU leg and record in Drive table.
5) Start soak: 15 min idle, 60 min step-load (30% -> 60% -> 90% target for 30s bursts), 15 min cooldown.
6) Confirm telemetry ingestion to metrics stack and automated throttle path to Redwood router.
7) Create incident channel and escalation contact in the rack doc.

Contingency play (if surge/trip detected):
- Automated: Router enforces per-tenant burst cap; redirect new sessions to dedicated region or lower-power model variant.
- Operator: Initiate spill to neighbor racks (configured via physical cross-connects), reduce rack-level clock limits, and schedule immediate tech swap for failed CDU.
- Comms: Notify Customer Success if customer-held workloads are impacted; use template notifs in CONFLUENCE:INFRA-RACKS-2026.

Open questions / known unknowns:
- Site-specific PUE data for colos in APAC (we used 1.25 general assumption) — action: request meter export (INFRA-4123).
- CDU redundancy pattern differs across partners: confirm whether local colo supports rapid inline swap without full power-down.
- Thermal probe calibration drift observed in prior installs — need calibration runbook.

Action items (owners):
- Marco Liu: collect APAC PUE and electrical single-line diagrams for next meeting (due 2026-03-09).
- Emily Chen: create a minimal dashboard template for soak runs (metrics + PDU legs + inlet temps) and PR the Grafana board (GH PR link in linked_artifacts).
- Samir Rodriguez: draft runbook section for "CDU failure during surge" and test tabletop with ops (due 2026-03-05).

Notes to self (informal):
- We should bake these margins directly into the platform routing decisions so that customers never hit hard breaker boundaries.
- Consider a thermal-aware placement policy in the scheduler that treats racks as first-class resources (inlet temp, recent surge history).

References & quick links:
- Confluence:INFRA-RACKS-2026 (design notes and prior postmortems)
- Jira:INFRA-4123 (APAC meter export)
- GH PR: repo/infrastructure/pull/228 (PDU firmware)

End of draft — this doc is intentionally informal and meant to be iterated with SRE and Field Ops.
